name: MiCS-5524 Gas Sensor
description: The `mics_5524` sensor platform allows you to use the **MiCS-5524** MEMS multi-gas sensor - the small 5 V analog modules with `VCC` / `GND` / `A0` / `EN` pads, and the DFRobot "Fermion" breakout they are cloned from - with ESPHome. One entry configures one physical sensor: it reads the analog output once per `update_interval` and publishes every gas listed under it as its own sub-sensor.

config_entries.label: Pin
config_entries.description:
**Required — set exactly one of:** `voltage`, `pin`.

The pin the AO output is connected to. The component creates the `adc` sensor it reads from and averages `sample_count:` conversions of it per reading. Exactly one of `voltage:` and `pin:` is required.

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval between two readings, shared by every gas of the entry. Defaults to `30s`.

config_entries.label: Air Reference
config_entries.description:
**Set at most one of:** `air_reference`, `r0`, `calibration`.

The fixed clean-air reference of the vendor model in volts (`VCC - V_AO` measured in clean air). It has to be smaller than `vcc:`, skips the calibration at boot, and is mutually exclusive with `calibration:` and `r0:`. Only accepted with `conversion: dfrobot`.

config_entries.label: Ammonia
config_entries.description: **Required — set at least one of:** `carbon_monoxide`, `hydrogen`, `ethanol`, `ammonia`, `methane`.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name for the sensor. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the sensor in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default device class of a sensor.

config_entries.label: Unit Of Measurement
config_entries.description: Manually set the unit of measurement the sensor should advertise its values with. This does not actually do any maths (conversion between units).

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals
config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.label: Coefficient A
config_entries.description: **Set together with:** `coefficient_b` (all-or-none).

config_entries.label: Coefficient B
config_entries.description: **Set together with:** `coefficient_a` (all-or-none).

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Expire After
config_entries.description: Manually set the time in which the sensor values should be marked as “expired”/“unknown”. Not providing any value means no expiry.

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: Specify filters to use for some basic transforming of values. See [Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/#sensor-filters) for more information.

config_entries.label: Force Update
config_entries.description: If true, this option will force the frontend (usually Home Assistant) to create a state changed event when the sensor updates even if the value stayed the same. Some applications like Grafana require this when working with Home Assistant, but beware it can significantly increase the database size. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: State Class
config_entries.description: The state class for the sensor. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#available-state-classes](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#available-state-classes) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default state class of a sensor.

config_entries.label: Calibration
config_entries.description:
**Set at most one of:** `air_reference`, `r0`, `calibration`.

Capture the clean-air reference at boot instead of hard-coding it (`air_reference:` or `r0:`). At most one of `calibration:`, `air_reference:` and `r0:` may be set.

config_entries.label: Delay
config_entries.description: The time to wait after boot before the first sample, so the module has settled. Defaults to `60s`.

config_entries.label: Persist
config_entries.description: Store the captured reference in flash so it survives a reboot. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Sample Count
config_entries.description: The number of readings averaged into the reference. Defaults to `10`. Range: 2-16.

config_entries.label: Sample Interval
config_entries.description: The spacing between two of those readings. Defaults to `20ms`; the minimum is 16 ms, one pass of the main loop.

config_entries.label: Enable Pin
config_entries.description: The pin wired to the `EN` pad of the module. The input is active low, so configure `inverted: true`, or the module stays asleep and every reading sits at 0 V.

config_entries.label: Mode
config_entries.description: Pin mode flags (input / output / pullup / pulldown / open_drain). Combine flags as needed — e.g. input + pullup for a button pulled to VCC.

config_entries.label: Input
config_entries.description: Set the input mode flag.

config_entries.label: Output
config_entries.description: Set the output mode flag.

config_entries.label: Pullup
config_entries.description: Set the pullup mode flag.

config_entries.label: Pulldown
config_entries.description: Set the pulldown mode flag.

config_entries.label: Open Drain
config_entries.description: Set the open drain mode flag.

config_entries.label: Inverted
config_entries.description: Invert the logical level. ``true`` swaps high/low in software so an active-low button reads as active when grounded.

config_entries.label: Voltage
config_entries.description:
**Required — set exactly one of:** `voltage`, `pin`.

The ID of a voltage sampler (`adc`, `ads1115`, ...) that reads the AO pin. Exactly one of `voltage:` and `pin:` is required.

config_entries.label: Voltage Divider
config_entries.description:
**Set at most one of:** `voltage_divider`, `voltage_multiplier`.

The resistor divider in front of the pin, from which the multiplier is derived as `(r1 + r2) / r2`. Mutually exclusive with `voltage_multiplier:`.

config_entries.label: R1
config_entries.description: The resistor between AO and the pin, in Ohm.

config_entries.label: R2
config_entries.description: The resistor between the pin and ground, in Ohm.

config_entries.label: Voltage Multiplier
config_entries.description:
**Set at most one of:** `voltage_divider`, `voltage_multiplier`.

The multiplier applied to the sampled voltage, the inverse of the divider ratio (`1.5` for a 10k/20k divider, `1.0` for a directly connected sensor or a sampler with a wider input range). Defaults to `1.0`. Mutually exclusive with `voltage_divider:`.

config_entries.label: Voltage Sensor
config_entries.description: The averaged, scaled AO voltage in V.

config_entries.description: The name for the sensor. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the sensor in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Device Class
config_entries.description: The device class for the sensor. See [https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor/#device-class) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default device class of a sensor.

config_entries.label: Unit Of Measurement
config_entries.description: Manually set the unit of measurement the sensor should advertise its values with. This does not actually do any maths (conversion between units).

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID for code generation. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Accuracy Decimals
config_entries.description: Set the number of digits after the decimal point that data consumers should use. While this does not change the value sent across the API, Home Assistant's ESPHome integration will round the value accordingly before using or storing it. The number of digits will also be used to set the entity's default display precision. Thus, one can display fewer decimals, but cannot increase precision of sensor values in Home Assistant. (The default value varies depending on component and sensor.)

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Expire After
config_entries.description: Manually set the time in which the sensor values should be marked as “expired”/“unknown”. Not providing any value means no expiry.

config_entries.label: Filters
config_entries.description: Specify filters to use for some basic transforming of values. See [Sensor Filters](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/#sensor-filters) for more information.

config_entries.label: Force Update
config_entries.description: If true, this option will force the frontend (usually Home Assistant) to create a state changed event when the sensor updates even if the value stayed the same. Some applications like Grafana require this when working with Home Assistant, but beware it can significantly increase the database size. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: State Class
config_entries.description: The state class for the sensor. See [https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#available-state-classes](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/sensor/#available-state-classes) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default state class of a sensor.

config_entries.label: ADC Attenuation
config_entries.description: The attenuation of the `adc` sensor that `pin:` creates: `0db`, `2.5db`, `6db`, `11db`, `12db` or `auto`. Defaults to `12db` on ESP32 so the pin is not clipped by the 0 dB default, and it also picks the default `adc_input_max:` of the wiring check there. With `voltage:` set `attenuation:` on that sampler instead.

config_entries.label: ADC Input Max
config_entries.description: The top of the measuring range of the sampler, in volts: the largest reading the wiring can produce (`vcc:` scaled by `voltage_divider:` or `voltage_multiplier:`) has to stay within it, and a 10 mV margin is allowed. Defaults to the built-in limit of the platform (ESP32 and RP2 `3.3`, ESP8266 `1.0`); for an ESP32 `pin:` source it defaults to the range of the configured `adc_attenuation:` instead. On a platform without a built-in limit both this and `adc_pin_max:` are required as soon as the wiring is checked.

config_entries.label: ADC Pin Max
config_entries.description: The absolute maximum the ADC pin tolerates, in volts; it is checked the same way as `adc_input_max:`. Defaults to the built-in limit of the platform (ESP32 and RP2 `3.6`, ESP8266 `1.0`).

config_entries.label: Conversion
config_entries.description: The conversion model of the sensor, `dfrobot` (default) or `datasheet`. See [How the Numbers Are Calculated](https://esphome.io/components/sensor/mics_5524/#how-the-numbers-are-calculated).

config_entries.label: Rl
config_entries.description: The load resistor `RL` of the datasheet model, in kΩ. Defaults to `10`. Only accepted with `conversion: datasheet`.

config_entries.label: Sample Count
config_entries.description: The number of AO conversions averaged per reading. They run back to back inside one pass of the main loop. Defaults to `4`. Range: 1-16.

config_entries.label: Vcc
config_entries.description: The supply voltage of the module. A reading above it cannot come from the sensor, so it is reported as `unknown` with a warning instead of being published as a measurement. Defaults to `5.0`.

config_entries.label: Warmup Time
config_entries.description: The heater warm-up. Nothing is published before it has elapsed. Defaults to `3min`; use `24h` for the burn-in of a new module.
